title: Ghost node decommission signal amplified by compatibility-hash mismatch causing cascading fallback surge
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2025-03-02 at ~15:21 UTC a rapid spike in fallback traffic and cross-region latency was observed, caused by a convergence of two rare conditions: truncated/de-duplicated decommission signals from a cloud maintenance window and a non-deterministic variant-compatibility hash that caused many worker pools to mark primary variants as incompatible. The combination produced a fast-moving cascade of drains and fallback routing that increased 99th percentile response latency by 3-4x and generated a sustained 2.8x token bill for the affected customers during the incident window.

What happened (timeline):
- 15:18 UTC: cloud provider maintenance rolled some host-level network updates in us-west-2. A subset of instance lifecycle notifications included truncated instance IDs (missing trailing suffix) in the cloud event payload that our drain-aggregator accepted.
- 15:20 UTC: drain-aggregator created multiple tombstone records with partial IDs that matched multiple live nodes due to substring matching heuristics. Tombstones propagated to the router cache faster than expected because TTL deduplication used the tombstone key directly.
- 15:22 UTC: router instances consulted the variant-compatibility table while deciding fallback targets. The compatibility table in production used a stable-but-unpinned hash function across deploys; a small rollout with different build-time seeds caused one pool of routers to calculate a different hash mapping for variant compatibility, marking several primary variants as incompatible.
- 15:23–15:40 UTC: combination of tombstones and mismatched compatibility mapping caused a rapid fan-out: requests routed away from primary variants into lower-cost variants across tiers, and backfilling created additional KV-cache misses that amplified throughput. Fallback rate increased by ~270% and sustained for ~20 minutes while reconciliations slowly converged.
- 15:45 UTC: alerting and on-call notifications triggered. Engineers applied emergency throttle and ran a fix to reconcile tombstones and force a deterministic compatibility table. Full corrective rollout completed 15:55 UTC.

Root causes: (1) overly-greedy tombstone matching: drain-aggregator accepted cloud lifecycle events with truncated IDs and used substring matching, producing ambiguous tombstones; (2) non-deterministic compatibility hash: compatibility matrix generation used a non-stable runtime seed across builds, so different router groups computed incompatible mappings; (3) lack of fast deduplication and repair: there was no quick path to merge tombstones or to reconcile variant compatibility across router pools before fallback amplification.

Immediate mitigations applied: 
- Switched drain-aggregator to strict exact-match on instance IDs and paused accepting lifecycle events from the problematic feed.
- Deployed a compatibility-table hotfix that forces a canonical hash function (sha256 with explicit salt) and propagated it with a rolling restart that preserves cache warm state.
- Enabled a temporary backpressure rule in the routing plane: if fallback rate for a route increases >200% in 2 minutes, cap the fallback throughput and keep a fraction pinned to primary variants.

Impact metrics: 
- Affected region: us-west-2 primarily, with cross-talk to us-west-1 via routing policies.
- Duration: ~37 minutes (15:18–15:55 UTC).
- Observed fallback increase: peak +270% above baseline.
- Latency: 99th p95 increased 3–4x for requests that hit fallback path; p50 unaffected.
- Cost: estimated additional token spend ~2.8x for customers routed through the affected tier during the window.

Where this ticket lives: postmortem + followups combined. See attachments for full artifacts.
comments: 2025-03-02 15:50 — Marco Chen: Emergency hotfix rolled to force deterministic compatibility table and strict ID matching. Initial telemetry looks stable; still watching for regressions.
2025-03-02 16:05 — Aisha Patel (PM): Noted customer-impacting spike. Eng to prepare a short customer-facing blurb for affected orgs; CS will pull metrics. Action: Aisha to coordinate with CS.
2025-03-03 09:10 — SRE: Added short-lived backpressure rule and adjusted alert thresholds to detect rapid fallback amplification sooner. Need follow-up to make this permanent in routing policy DSL.

2025-03-04 11:30 — Baz Liu (Infra): Found that the cloud event parser library silently trimmed trailing whitespace during a dependency bump which exposed the truncated-ID feed. Raised an immediate patch in our event consumer to validate formats.

2025-03-06 14:00 — Design feedback (Ruth Gomez): Dashboard needs a focused fallback surge panel that correlates tombstone velocity with variant compatibility flips; created a mock in Figma linked in attachments.

resolution_summary: Fixed parser to validate full instance IDs, tightened tombstone matching to exact IDs, deployed deterministic compatibility-table generation, and added temporary fallback backpressure. Incident closed after monitoring confirmed stable fallback rates and restored latency to baseline.
retrospective_actions: Add strict schema validation and umask tests to lifecycle event consumer (owner: Infra, estimate: 3)
Implement tombstone deduplication and a fast merge job to repair ambiguous tombstones (owner: Routing, estimate: 5)
Pin compatibility-table hash function and add CI check to assert deterministic outputs across builds (owner: Runtime, estimate: 3)
Add routing DSL rule to permanently limit fallback fan-out and expose config in Console (owner: Console, estimate: 8)
Create chaos test that injects truncated events and variant-mismatch scenarios for the staging routing plane (owner: SRE, estimate: 5)
Customer communication: short incident note and billing review for affected customers (owner: CS + PM, due: 2025-03-16)
